authority.owner_confirmation: 12 November: Designer recommendations adopted. 13 November: one Hold button, breakage costs time not food, 50/200/150 ms timing, and an unblocked drop onto the Panel operator loses the Task; only Panel can kill and still deliver.
authority.latest_recorded_owner_decisions: docs/design/owner-decisions.md at 9bb497948861521030c37a8d2c60a6318f1745c9; includes hunger order, remaining timing, and no slower mode for now.

precedence: Apply these owner-confirmed Food decisions over conflicting Food proposals only. Inherit unsuperseded parent rules; do not globally alter ordinary attacks, role allowances, offices, navigation, medical rules or versioned setup. Earlier Food highlights are historical evidence, not parallel active rules.

decisions.rule: One exclusive Food Supply step at the start of each round, after any Captain election and before PRE_TURN. At most one Task starts per round; no concurrent Tasks. Skip when fewer than two players qualify. Asking lasts 30000 ms. A request made within it keeps its full 15000 ms answer interval. Without a Task, close after asking and any timely outstanding answer interval. Ordinary turns, movement, shots, Hack, votes and Captain commands are unavailable during the step.

The Volunteer and Partner are two distinct living players outside Hospital and Jail, neither of whom participated in the preceding round's Food Task. These requirements are authoritative, not inferred from a phone's appearance.

One outstanding Partner request at a time; the first to reach the server counts. Request and answer are private to those two players. Others receive only the anonymous someone-is-asking state. The Partner may join or decline within 15000 ms. No answer is decline; withdrawal is refusal. Join, withdrawal and expiry are serialized by the server, with only one accepted terminal result.

After a refusal another eligible Volunteer may ask while the original asking interval remains open. The refused Volunteer cannot ask again this round but may be asked as Partner. Starting a Task records both participants as excluded from next round's Food step, whether delivered, lost or cancelled. A refusal does not trigger that next-round exclusion. No lifetime Food Task initiation limit applies; this rule does not extend to the separately undesigned Engine Task.

The server assigns Winch and Panel randomly when the Task starts. The Winch has one Hold button: finger down lifts/holds the crate and finger up releases it. The prototype calls these inputs raise/lower; it does not authorize two separate buttons or a production command schema. Panel controls horizontal Release/Lock. A wrong-place release breaks the crate; a replacement must be fetched from the intake within the remaining Task time. Breakage consumes no food and does not reset the deadline. Task travel consumes no voluntary movement. No separate attack, arming, confirmation or escape input is added. The Supply Room is not an ordinary movement destination.

The complete Task lasts 30000 ms from authoritative start, including a 4000 ms briefing. The panel clicks stop to stop: 50 ms snap then 200 ms rest, with 150 ms warning margin. Lock takes the stop at rest or the destination stop during its snap. The approved lift, fall, swing and collision constants are in approved_parameters. These numbers are not evidence of real-network safety or equivalent timing access. There is no slower mode for now, as the owner decided after practice; revisit through playtesting, not a per-client timing change.

Task hazards arise from ordinary crane controls: letting the crate drop on the Panel operator or a Lock at the Winch cab. An unblocked lethal input eliminates immediately without Hospital admission. Task kills, including mistakes, are not attacks and never read or spend an ordinary attack opportunity; repeated participation creates no Task kill quota.

Read applicable existing Protection at each lethal resolution. It stops the hazard and is consumed under its existing activation/use rules. Without applicable Protection, the server's safety catch stops that lethal press with 25% probability. Clone does not apply. Protection and lucky catches have identical participant feedback, with no cause, role, grantor or defensive resource disclosed. Server randomness and Protection consumption must be retained once with the resolved result.

An unblocked crate drop onto the Panel operator breaks the crate and loses the Task. The Winch has no kill-and-deliver recovery path. Only the Panel can kill and still deliver: cut after the crate has landed and then turn the surviving Panel operator's key. Other deaths without a valid delivery position lose the Task. Both living operators turn their keys for ordinary delivery; a legitimate survivor uses their own key. Applicable Protection or lucky stops remain stops, not kills. This intentionally supersedes the previous two-sided survivor paths; the proposed brake continuation is not automatically adopted.

A living participant's disconnect has 8000 ms grace while the Task and hazards continue. Reconnection within grace does not pause, restart or reset it. Expired grace cancels; already-resolved deaths remain. A dead participant's connection does not cancel the survivor's eligible continuation. Deliberate leaving has no extra penalty. Ended results and deliveries cannot be repeated or undone by reconnect, retry or late timeout processing.

Both participants return at startedAt + 32500 ms for every outcome, including early success, loss, death and cancellation. Restore each recorded starting place; a killed participant is shown Eliminated there. No outside movement or forced transfer runs during this exclusive step, so those places remain reserved. Outcome timing must not shorten or extend public absence.

Only the participants see the Supply Room, control effects, warnings, keys, timer and their partner's alive/offline state. Others may infer participants from their vacant board places and see a generic two-away banner. Do not send others a Task result, killer, hazard kind, Protection cause or private refusal. Public result information is the food count and normal board death/return status; accepted social deduction from those observations remains possible.

Initial stock is five packages, two doses per package. A successful delivery adds five packages, exactly once. Stock is public in packages, including half-package changes. Show the warning whenever one package or less remains. A non-delivery adds nothing and emits no public Task-result message.

At the end of each player's own ordinary turn, including Pass and timeout, each living player outside Hospital consumes one dose. Jail prisoners eat; Hospital patients do not. With insufficient stock, recorded ordinary turn order determines who eats. The server performs consumption; an omitted, delayed or replayed ship-life visit cannot affect it. A private Hack continuation is not a second ordinary turn end.

A player unable to eat becomes hungry. At the end of the round, after whole-reality Sync and the retained attacks/actions, but before Rescue, process retained hunger in recorded turn order. A living Healthy hungry player becomes Injured and enters Hospital under inherited rules. An already Injured or Eliminated player receives no additional consequence: no extra hit, revival or injury-deadline extension. Hunger is not an attack; Protection and Clone do not stop it. A newly hunger-injured player can receive Rescue from the next round; do not create a same-round post-hunger Rescue opportunity. Existing valid Rescue for an already Injured patient remains governed by inherited rules. Preserve four beds, permanent overflow elimination, detention and the full following-round rescue deadline.

No Blackhole is active during Food Supply: it precedes PRE_TURN activation. All subsequently created realities inherit the completed Task state, including deaths, consumed Protection, delivery and participation. Branching does not refill anything. Meals, remaining food and hunger are reality-local. Sync retains the selected whole reality's inventory and hunger, including inherited consumption, and discards the others without recombining effects and costs. Hunger resolves only afterward.

Preserve the predecessor's audience model during branching: players receive authorized state for their reality and the shared display retains its labeled finalized checkpoint. Public food information does not authorize branch identifiers, branch counts, unselected-world stock or speculative shared outcomes. Requests, receipts, Protection, randomness and private refusals retain their specified audiences.

This is an inactive successor candidate for new matches only after contract and integration acceptance. Existing matches retain exact saved protocol/engine/ruleset/art/setup pins and payloads. Optional Original Powers stay as previously configured. No Studio save, design merge or candidate record changes live authority. No Engine Task is specified or enabled here.

remaining_proposed_hold_behaviors.intake_return: Release over the intake returns the crate intact rather than breaking it.
remaining_proposed_hold_behaviors.moving_platform: Landing requires the panel to be locked; a release over a moving platform breaks the crate.
remaining_proposed_hold_behaviors.early_hold: A finger already down lifts automatically as soon as the hook is eligible over the crate.
remaining_proposed_hold_behaviors.stopped_drop_brake: After a protected or lucky stopped drop the brake holds the crate until the next Hold takes it back.

contract_review_requirement: Do not port the blanket lower-is-never-stale exception. Support release during an unacknowledged Hold with durable gesture identity/order, crate/task binding and idempotent receipts. A release received first must prevent an older late Hold from resurrecting it. A release for an old gesture must not release a new one. Exact payload and presence/recovery semantics remain subject to contract acceptance.
